snippet.title: 'Grey's Anatomy's' Eric Dane says he has 'one functioning arm' after ALS diagnosis in new interview
snippet.description:
The “Grey’s Anatomy” and “Euphoria” star tells ABC News’ Diane Sawyer about the moment he received his diagnosis about the incurable disease and how the symptoms have progressed.

He is speaking out for the first time in a television interview about his battle with ALS, a degenerative neurological disorder.

"I wake up every day and I'm immediately reminded that this is happening," Dane, 52, said in an interview with Diane Sawyer that aired Monday on "Good Morning America." "It's not a dream."

Just a few months after first revealing his ALS diagnosis publicly in April, Dane said he has lost function of his right arm and worries about what's next.

Eric Dane, the face behind the world’s favorite plastic surgeon, Mark “McSteamy” Sloan, has been a heartthrob since the moment he stepped into the industry. There’s just something about his effortless charm, confidence, and the way he would command any scene he was in. Years after his exit from Grey’s Anatomy, the fans still beg for him to return and walk through those hospital doors one more time. But behind all the fame, the actor has fought battles that no one has seen. 

From addiction to depression to a total collapse of his personal life, Dane has been through quite a journey. And just when he was starting to rebuild himself at 53, his latest diagnosis has changed everything. Forever.

snippet.title: Early Signs of ALS: Eric Dane’s Story & Why Early Detection Matters #als #ericdane #healthline
snippet.description:
How much do you know about the early signs of ALS?

The world continues to reflect on the legacy of Eric Dane, beloved for his role on Grey's Anatomy. After publicly sharing his ALS diagnosis, he used his voice to raise awareness about a disease that still challenges modern medicine.

Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) — also known as Lou Gehrig’s disease — is a progressive neurological condition that attacks the nerve cells controlling voluntary muscle movement.

⚠️ Early symptoms may include:

Muscle twitching (fasciculations)

Weakness in arms or legs

Slurred speech

Difficulty swallowing

Loss of coordination

In nearly 90% of cases, the exact cause remains unknown. While there is currently no cure, early diagnosis and a multidisciplinary care team can significantly improve quality of life and symptom management.

snippet.title: Eric Dane Said This Before He Died Peacefully 😭💔
snippet.description:
‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Eric Dane Spoke About His Health Before Death😭

Actor Eric Dane has died of complications related to ALS on Thursday, People reports. He was 53.

Dane’s family confirmed his death with a statement sharing that he had “spent his final days surrounded by dear friends, his devoted wife, and his two beautiful daughters, Billie and Georgia, who were the center of his world.”

The actor, known for his roles in Grey’s Anatomy and Euphoria, revealed his battle with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, or ALS, in April 2025. In the months since publicly sharing his illness, he advocated for others.

“Throughout his journey with ALS, Eric became a passionate advocate for awareness and research, determined to make a difference for others facing the same fight,” the statement continues. “He will be deeply missed, and lovingly remembered always. Eric adored his fans and is forever grateful for the outpouring of love and support he’s received. The family has asked for privacy as they navigate this impossible time.”

In a June 2025 interview with Diane Sawyer, Dane opened up about his early symptoms, noting that he initially experienced weakness in his right hand. “I didn't really think anything of it at the time — I thought maybe I'd been texting too much, or my hand was fatigued,” he said. However, after nine months and multiple visits to hand specialists and neurologists, the actor received the diagnosis. By June 2025, he had lost use of his right side.

“I'm angry because, you know, my father was taken from me when I was young, and now, you know, there's a very good chance I'm going to be taken from my girls while they're very young,” Dane told Sawyer of his dad. “I mean, really at the end of the day, all I want to do is spend time with my family and work a little bit if I can.”

In the interview, he shared that he was in a research study for ALS and was taking medication that left him “hopeful.”

Dane began his acting career in the ‘90s with guest roles in TV shows like Saved by the Bell,The Wonder Years and Married…with Children.

In 2006, he joined ABC’s medical drama Grey’s Anatomy as Dr. Mark Sloan, nicknamed “McSteamy.” He joined the main cast in Season 3 and appeared until his character’s death in a plane crash in Season 9. He briefly returned as a guest star via a dream sequence in Season 17.

Dane went on to star in The Last Ship post Grey's Anatomy, which was followed a crew on a Navy ship that must find a cure for the pandemic that wiped out humanity. It aired on TNT from 2014 to 2018.

In 2019, Dane took on the scene-stealing role of badly behaving suburban father Cal Jacobs in HBO’s Euphoria. He appeared on the show for its first two seasons, which aired in 2019 and 2022. He then returned to set for the show’s long-awaited third season in 2025.

Though best known for his TV work, Dane’s film roles included X-Men: The Last Stand, Marley & Me, Dangerous Waters and Bad Boys: Ride or Die. He reunited with Euphoria co-star Sydney Sweeney for the 2025 release Americana.

Dane was married to actress Rebecca Gayheart, with whom he shared daughters Billie Beatrice, 15, and Georgia Geraldine, 13. The spouses filed for divorce in 2018, however, in March 2025, Gayheart called off the proceedings. He told Sawyer of their relationship, “We have managed to become better friends and better parents, and she is probably my biggest champion, my most stalwart supporter.”

Rest in power king

snippet.title: Eric Dane’s Widow Rebecca Gayheart Breaks Her Silence After His Death
snippet.description: Eric Dane’s widow Rebecca Gayheart is sharing her first words since his death last week from ALS, this as tributes continue to pour in from his friends and former castmates. Rebecca shared that she is “blown away” but the “outpouring of love and support from the community.” Within hours of his death, Erics last interview was streaming on Netflix in “Famous Last Words.” “Extra” spoke to Brad Falchuck, who filmed the inspiring heart-to-heart with Eric back in November.

snippet.title: What to Know About The Passing of Eric Dane and ALS
snippet.description:
Sad to hear about Eric Dane’s passing yesterday. I grew up watching Grey’s Anatomy, and like many people in medicine, that show inspired part of my journey into healthcare. Losing someone to ALS at 53 is a reminder of how devastating this disease can be.

ALS is a progressive neurological condition that affects the motor neurons controlling movement. It doesn’t usually affect awareness or intelligence, which makes the progression especially tragic. There is still no cure, and research and awareness matter. 

May Eric Dane rest in peace 🙏

snippet.title: Eric Dane’s FINAL WORDS to Daughters in Secret Last Interview: ‘You Are My Everything’
snippet.description: The late Eric Dane is speaking out in a new Netflix special “Famous Last Words,” in a secret interview he did to be released after his death. His voice is halting and broken, but his spirit remained unbroken as he bravely battled ALS. Interviewed by Gwyneth Paltrow’s producer husband Brad Falchuk, Eric reflected on his deep love for ex Rebecca Gayheart and shared an emotional final message to his teenage daughters.
